issues.issue: The Certificate Factor is computed for 'any Class of Regular Certificates' from Certificate Principal Balance, with a parenthetical carve-out only for the Class C Certificates' Notional Amount, yet the definition of Class Principal Balance states that the Interest Only Certificates have no principal balance. For the Class X-1, X-2 and XW Certificates the fraction has no numerator.

The Agreement defines the Certificate Insurance Policy as including 'any endorsements thereto,' while the Policy itself provides that it sets forth in full Financial Security's undertaking and 'shall not be modified, altered or affected by any other agreement or instrument.' Whether the PSA's terms about the Policy can enlarge or qualify the insurer's obligation must be resolved between the two documents.

The Certificate Insurer Fee Rate is subtracted from the Net Rate Cap of the Insured Certificates under the Net Rate Cap definition and is also the measure of the Premium Distribution Amount payable out of the waterfall under Section 4.02. Whether the premium is borne once or twice, and by whom, only emerges from reading those provisions together.

The proviso that an Insured Certificate's Certificate Principal Balance 'shall be deemed not to be reduced by any principal amounts paid to the Holder thereof from payments made by the Certificate Insurer' operates 'solely for purposes of' the Premium Distribution Amount and the insurer's subrogation rights, leaving unclear what the balance is for every other purpose, including loss allocation and voting. The deemed-balance device is the point at which the insurer's and the holders' entitlements diverge.

This definition makes the Holder the person registered in the Certificate Register, but Section 12.01 provides for the Certificate Insurer to exercise the voting rights of the Holders of the Insured Certificates. Who counts as the consenting Holder of an Insured Certificate cannot be answered from this definition alone.

After identifying reimbursement 'with interest' for claims paid, the definition adds 'any amounts with respect to the Class 1-A-3 Certificates owing to the Certificate Insurer and remaining unpaid,' an open-ended catch-all not tied to any enumerated obligation. The class of amounts it sweeps in is unbounded.

The closing phrase 'any amounts with respect to the Class 2-A-3 Certificates owing to the Certificate Insurer and remaining unpaid' is a general catch-all appended to the specific reimbursement-with-interest item. Nothing in the definition limits what obligations qualify as 'owing.'

The clause 'any amounts with respect to the Class 4-A-2 Certificates owing to the Certificate Insurer and remaining unpaid' extends the reimbursement amount beyond the enumerated claims paid under the Policy without any stated boundary. Its scope against the specific preceding item is open to construction.

The Collection Account is maintained by the Master Servicer in its own name, yet the last sentence says it 'may be deemed to be a sub-account of the Distribution Account,' which the Distribution Account definition places with the Trust Administrator in the name of the Trustee. Whose account it is, and on what conditions the deeming operates, requires reading the two definitions together.

The two limbs run together without punctuation ('should be directed With respect to the Trust Administrator'), and the Trust Administrator is given one address 'for certificate transfer purposes' and another 'for all other purposes.' Which office a given notice must reach is left to be sorted out.

The Countrywide Mortgage Loans are identified by loans showing 'Countrywide Home Loans Servicing L.P.' as Servicer, whereas the defined term 'Countrywide' means Countrywide Home Loans, Inc. The two entities are not the same and the definitions do not reconcile them.

The definition is expressed 'solely with respect to the Countrywide Serviced Mortgage Loans,' a term the Agreement never defines (it defines 'Countrywide Mortgage Loans'). The loans to which the Servicing Agreement applies must therefore be inferred.

The fee is computed on 'the Scheduled Principal Balance of the Mortgage Loans,' but the Agreement defines 'Stated Principal Balance' and 'Principal Balance,' not 'Scheduled Principal Balance.' The multiplicand of the fee is undefined.

Current Interest is defined only 'with respect to each Class of Offered Certificates,' yet the Available Funds Rate Cap definition subtracts 'the Current Interest for the Class X-1, Class X-2 and Class XW Certificates,' none of which are Offered Certificates as the Preliminary Statement defines that term. The two provisions cannot both be given their literal effect.

The trigger is 'the product of (i) 28.15% and the Senior Enhancement Percentage for any Distribution Date prior to ... and (ii) 35.15% and the Senior Enhancement Percentage' — a single 'product of' governing two alternative time periods joined by 'and.' Whether the two limbs are alternatives or multiplicands is not clear from the wording.
